title: Fully Nonlinear Elliptic Regularity (Evans-Krylov)
description: Formalizes the extension of Hilbert's 19th problem to fully nonlinear elliptic equations. Defines fully nonlinear elliptic operators with uniform ellipticity conditions, proves properties of Pucci extremal operators (M⁺ ≤ M⁻, superadditivity, sign cases, uniform ellipticity), establishes a viscosity solution framework with touching functions, and states the Evans-Krylov theorem (C^{2,α} regularity for convex uniformly elliptic equations). Proves the full regularity chain: Evans-Krylov + Schauder bootstrap = C^∞ for smooth convex F.

meta.author: Formalized in Lean 4 (Mathlib)
originalContributions: Fully nonlinear operator framework with ellipticity constants (λ, Λ)
Pucci extremal operators in 1D with proved bounds (M⁻ ≤ M⁺, superadditivity)
Pucci maximal operator proved uniformly elliptic (all sandwich bounds)
Viscosity solution definitions (sub/super/solution) with touching functions
Evans-Krylov + Schauder regularity chain (proved from axioms)
Bellman equation convexity (sup of affine is convex, proved)

references.title: Classical solutions of fully nonlinear, convex, second-order elliptic equations
Boundedly nonhomogeneous elliptic and parabolic equations

overview.historicalContext: Hilbert's 19th problem (1900) asked whether variational minimizers are always smooth. De Giorgi and Nash (1957-58) resolved this for divergence-form equations. The Evans-Krylov theorem (1982) extended the positive answer to fully nonlinear convex equations.
overview.problemStatement: Does the regularity theory of Hilbert's 19th problem extend to fully nonlinear equations F(D²u) = 0? Answer: Yes, when F is convex/concave and uniformly elliptic (Evans-Krylov).
overview.proofStrategy: Define fully nonlinear operators with uniform ellipticity, formalize Pucci extremal operators as canonical bounds, define viscosity solutions, state Evans-Krylov as axiom, and prove the regularity chain from Evans-Krylov through Schauder bootstrap to full smoothness.
keyInsights: Pucci operators M⁺, M⁻ bound all uniformly elliptic operators with given constants
Viscosity solutions are the correct weak solution concept for fully nonlinear PDEs
Convexity of F is essential: Nadirashvili-Vladut showed C^{2,α} fails without it
The regularity chain: ABP → Krylov-Safonov (C^α) → Evans-Krylov (C^{2,α}) → Schauder (C^∞)

sections.title: Fully Nonlinear Operators
sections.summary: Defines FullyNonlinearOp1D, monotonicity (degenerate ellipticity), and uniform ellipticity with sandwich bounds. Proves uniform ellipticity implies monotonicity.

sections.title: Pucci Extremal Operators
sections.summary: Defines M⁺ and M⁻ in 1D. Proves zero evaluation, M⁻ ≤ M⁺, superadditivity, sign cases, and that M⁺ is uniformly elliptic.

sections.title: Viscosity Solutions
sections.summary: Defines touching from above/below, viscosity sub/supersolutions, and viscosity solutions. Proves reflexivity of touching and uniqueness from comparison.

sections.title: Evans-Krylov Theorem
sections.summary: States the Evans-Krylov theorem (C^{2,α} for convex uniformly elliptic F) and Schauder bootstrap. Proves the full regularity chain.

sections.title: Applications and Counterexamples
sections.summary: Bellman equations (convex), Isaacs equations (not convex), Nadirashvili-Vladut counterexample, De Giorgi system counterexample.

conclusion.summary: The fully nonlinear extension of Hilbert's 19th problem is resolved affirmatively for convex/concave F (Evans-Krylov 1982). Non-convex case has counterexamples (Nadirashvili-Vladut 2008). 503 lines, 1 sorry, 8 axioms for deep PDE theory.
openQuestions: Can Evans-Krylov be proved for broader classes beyond convex/concave?
What is the optimal Holder exponent α in Evans-Krylov?
Can viscosity solution theory be formalized in Mathlib?
